Unconventional: Yes
County: Allegheny
Municipality: Forward Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/04/2026
Comments: An onsite inspection of the Fetchen MON197H16 well was conducted by OGI Pat Hiles. Act 9 sign is posted on the entrance of the lease road. ERP was located in the mailbox. properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2019-07-05 to Xto Energy Inc in Chapman Twp, Clinton county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Xto Energy Inc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2019-06-10
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 854943
Permit API: 035-21217
Unconventional: Yes
County: Clinton
Municipality: Chapman Twp
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 2019-07-05
Comments: Water samples collected on 5/28/2019 at the XTO Energy PA Tract 8546 Pad A as part of Complaint No. 342466, documented in Inspection Report 2886516, were received on 6/28/2019. The results indicate the seep off the West edge of the pad contained elevated levels of chloride and strontium, which indicates the fluid was a pollutional substance. Results from a sample of the same seep, collected by XTO Energy on 5/16/2019 and received on 7/3/2019 from XTO Energy, are consistent with the Department's results. The release of a pollutional substance outside of containment are a violation of section 402(b) of the Clean Streams Law, 78a.56(a), and Section 301 of the Solid Waste Management Act. The failure to report the release of a pollutional substance is a violation of 78a.66(b). Due to the unknown extent, material, and volume of the release, the Department recommends that XTO Energy remediate under Act 2. Outstanding violations associated with this permit refer to the grease spill that was investigated on 6/10/19. New violations are cited to well permit 035-21316.

Comments: Onsite for a routine inspection. The well is equipped to produce with a pump jack, rods, tubing, and an electric motor with a belt. The Department requests that the operator voluntarily cease the unauthorized discharge of all production fluids.Violations are cited

Violation ID: 8198420
Permit API: 125-29100
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: Cecil Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 8/13/2024
Comments: The Department conducted an inspection of this well on 8/13/2024 after being notified by Range that the production casing failed during stimulation activities. At the time of the inspection equipment was being mobilized off site, and stimulation activities were completed. According to Range, anomalously low treatment pressures were observed while fraccing stage 64 of the 6H on 8/9/2024 at 7:17am. The Operator cut sand and started to flush when the low pressures were observed, and kill plugs were then placed in the production casing at 6531' and 6426'. A pressure of 2801 psi was observed on the backside of the production casing during the incident. Per Range, no anomalous pressures were observed on other casing annuli, nor were anomalous pressures observed on other offset wells. Range informed the Department during the inspection that the issue appears to be above the kill plug locations, and a log was scheduled to be run later in the week to determine the location of the failure. - The Department was not notified of the incident until 8/12/2024 at 3:45pm. This is a violation of 78a.73(c) which requires immediate notification to the Department in the event that anomalous pressures are observed during stimulation activities. - According to Range, a failure of the production casing was the cause of the observed anomalous treatment pressures. The failure of the production casing during stimulation is a violation of 78a.73(a). - The Department requests that Range submit as part of their Notice of Violation response a copy of the logs that are scheduled to be run that will be used to determine the location of the production casing failure. The Department also requests copies of stimulation records for stages 54 through stage 64 for the 6H.

Comments: On February 6, 2023, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted an incident response inspection (CTS 369753) at the EQT ARO LLC Elbow Fish and Game Club Pad A. Over the weekend, a line froze that is associated with one of EQT's gas dehydration units causing a pressure relief valve to open resulting in a release of glycol onto the pad surface. The triethylene glycol misted out of the relief valve and impacted a 40 ft. x 25 ft. area around the dehydration unit. At the time of arrival, EQT contractors were wiping glycol off of surrounding equipment. The contractors were beginning to excavate the southeast end of the dehydration unit. EQT is unsure of the amount of glycol that spilled outside of the secondary containment so, EQT plans to remediate the spill under ACT 2.The spilling of glycol outside of containment to the well pad surface is a violation of Clean Streams Law 402(b), Solid Waste Management Act Section 301, and Chapter 78a.56(a).

Comments: On April 13 2026, the Department conducted a follow up inspection of the CFR USX 5 OG Well in regards to violations issued under inspection report 4157445. Accompanying me in today's inspection is Rosie Wise (PaDEP)The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspection, the Department again observed the water flowing onto the access road. It did not appear any remedial actions have been taken to address the flowing water and resulting erosion and sedimentation issues on the access road.As previously described in IR 4157445:The water was observed flowing down the access road where it appeared to end at the well site. Erosion channels appear to have formed along the access road as a result of the flowing water. The water appears to be originating from a drainage channel/tributary to Antram Run. It appears that a culvert located under the access road may be damaged or obstructed, causing the water to flow onto the access road rather than through the culvert. The Department was unable to locate/inspect the culvert inlet. However, no water was observed discharging from the culvert outlet.Upon inspection of the well posting, it appeared a new well posting has been installed on a piece of the production equipment in accordance with OGA3211(H). The well posting appeared to contain the well permit number, operator's name, and operator's phone number. However, it did not appear to contain the operator's address. The Department recommends the operator ensure all required information is properly posted in accordance with OGA3211(G).Based on today's inspection, OGA3211(H) is being closed. All other violations issued in IR 4157445 remain outstanding.

properties.summary: Administrative violation issued on 4/03/2025 to TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC in Sugar Grove Township, Warren county. OGA3211(H) - WELL PERMITS - LABELING - Failure to install, in a permanent manner, the permit number on a completed well.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC
Violation Type: Administrative
Violation Date: 4/03/2025
Violation Code: OGA3211(H) - WELL PERMITS - LABELING - Failure to install, in a permanent manner, the permit number on a completed well.
Violation ID: 8227915
Permit API: 123-47902
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Sugar Grove Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/03/2025
Comments: The R H Stevenson Lease 4 conventional well is the nearest conventional well in proximity to the tank battery on the R H Stevenson lease. The tank battery is situated within earthen containment and consists of an upper level containing two stock tanks, and a lower level containing two polyurethane tanks. The stock tanks are plumbed into PVC piping that extends along the rear of the upper level of the earthen containment until terminating into the first of the two polyurethane tanks in the lower level. The first of the two polyurethane tanks in the lower level is also equipped with additional PVC piping apparently for the purpose of either removing or depositing fluids into the tank in the lower level of containment. At the time of this inspection, standing pools of fluid present in the upper level of the containment were found to have specific conductance measuring 5,980 microSiemens per centimeter (uS/cm). It was observed that straw had been laid down beneath the PVC piping in the upper level of containment. Where the straw cover ends, fluid was found to be actively flowing from the upper level of containment to the lower level. No fluid was observed to be flowing through the PVC piping connecting the stock tanks to the polyurethane tank during the time of this inspection. Neither polyurethane stock tank was found to have a noticeable volume of fluids contained within them at the time of this inspection. Some accumulation of fluids and crude oil could be observed around the base of the polyurethane tanks in the lower level of the containment at the time of this inspection. The flow of fluids from the upper level to the lower level of containment was not found to be accumulating nor increasing the accumulated volume of fluids and crude oil present at the bottom of the lower level of the containment at the time of this inspection.Approximately 40 feet south of the lower level tank battery containment area, crude oil and production fluids emerged on the soil surface. This flow of fluids continues west and is visually impacted by crude oil for approximately 180 feet. From there, soils and standing fluid with elevated specific conductance continue for approximately 75 feet before reaching a culvert. A pool of fluid at the entrance of the culvert was found to have specific conductance measuring 6,820 uS/cm.From the culvert, the fluid continues southwest in the natural swale for approximately 115 feet before reaching a point at which the swale transitions to an unnamed tributary (UNT) stream of Jackson Run, with defined bed and banks. At this point, waters in the UNT had specific conductance measuring 5,510 uS/cm. Specific conductance of 2,750 uS/cm was observed in the waters of the UNT in the remaining approximately 180 foot stretch, at which point there is a confluence with a second UNT of Jackson Run. Immediately before the confluence, waters in the impacted stream with specific conductance of 1,923 uS/cm were observed. Approximately two feet downstream of the confluence at a point with coordinates 41.95555, -79.29740 was the apparent end of impact to the UNTs of Jackson Run, where waters in the stream had a measured specific conductance of 42.6 uS/cm.At the time of this inspection, the well name, API number, and operator contact information was not displayed anywhere on the well.On 04/04/25 I called and spoke with William Cenk and Kyle Miller of Trinity Mineral Partners, LLC to request that the source and extent of the release be identified to prevent further pollution. Mr. Cenk and Mr. Miller agreed to meet with Department officials onsite next week. A Notice of Violations (NOV) is included as part of this inspection. Please refer to the NOV for additional information regarding cleanup expectations.

Violation ID: 8184780
Permit API: 125-22544
Unconventional: No
County: Washington

Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/25/2024
Comments: On April 25, 2024, inspection conducted at the US Natural Resources 1-P085 well site in Somerset Township, Washington County. This inspection follows up to IR 3744557, which documents the Department's response to a spill that reportedly occurred on April 10, 2024, when the onsite brine tank overfilled with production fluid and pushed a grease-like layer sitting on top of this fluid out the top of the tank onto the ground below. Present at this inspection were KPI representative Joel Grecko and myself. Mr. Grecko reports that remediation of the impacted area was completed on April 16, 2024. The following was observed:The access road appeared to be stable at the time of inspection with no observed evidence of accelerated erosion or sedimentation (see photo 1). Tire rutting was observed in the well site at the time of inspection (see photo 2). The area impacted by the grease-like substance was excavated with no staining observed in this area (see photo 3). No elevated soil conductivity was detected in this area, underneath the brine tank valve, or within the majority of the earthen berm surrounding the brine tank (see photos 4, 6, 7, 8, and 9). An area of slightly elevated conductivity was detected in the southwestern corner of the earthen berm surrounding the brine tank (see photos 5 and 9). However, no staining, distressed vegetation, or other visual impacts were observed in this area. The well head was equipped with a well tag, and no staining or distressed vegetation was observed on the ground around it (see photos 10 and 11). The operator's information was posted on the meter box (see photo 13). The brine tank appeared to be sound at the time of inspection, with any remaining grease-like substances appearing to have wiped off (see photo 14). Mr. Grecko was conducting brush clearing onsite when the Department arrived. Based on observations from this inspection, the Department recommends that maintenance is conducted on the well site (and on the access road, if needed) now that remediation is complete to address the aforementioned tire rutting. The Department recommends that the operator assess and evaluate the area of elevated conductivity in the earthen berm, as the conductivity reading taken in this location is an outlier when compared to other soil conductivity readings taken onsite. Finally the Department recommends that the remediated area is mulched and seeded until 70 percent vegetative growth coverage is achieved. The Department requests a response to this inspection report from the operator with the waste manifest from remediation included in this response, when available.Violations shall be noted and immediately corrected.

Comments: On February 22, 2024, the Department conducted a routine inspection. Access road is inaccessible and for a stretch, is under 1-2 feet of water (Photo 2). The Department recommends improving the access road. Portions of the access road and site appear to be within a wetland. Well appears equipped for production. Well is tagged and posted with previous and new operator; pending the transfer currently under review by the Department, the "previous" operator, Questa Petro Co, remains operator at this time according to Department records.Production tank appears to be structurally sound at this time, but appears to be sinking into the ground surface causing it to lean. Hissing sounds were observed by the Department coming from two points of the well equipment: at a pipe that extends from the smaller vertical tank (Photo 8) and behind the well tag in the center of Photo 9. Referring to Department OGIs. Discolored mud is observed under well equipment, along fencing, and extending off site. Specific conductivity readings were recorded on site to assess for the possibility of a brine release on site: -Background (Photo 15): 151.3 uSiemens-Under small vertical tank (Photo 13): 613 uSiemens-Under well tag (Photo 14): 672 uSiemensThese readings indicate that a brine release has occurred on site. The Department recommends removing all impacted soil and properly disposing. The Department requests that the quantity released, composition of fluids released, how the release occurred, and when the release occurred is included in the NOV response. The Department requests disposal documents of the impacted material removed from the site, when made available. Violations issued for brine release.

Violation ID: 8268728
Permit API: 015-23994
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Pike Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 3/25/2026
Comments: On 03/24/2026 at 1132 hours Repsol reported (CTS#396090) that at 0600 hours they noticed fluid in the southside ditch of the Ugliuzza well pad that was going towards the catch basin. There was a hose that did not have a cap on it and the fluid was coming from the hose. They are estimating ~630 gallons (1 barrel=42 gallons) of produced water was released off containment. Resource Management was contracted to conduct remediation. At ~1525 hours Repsol contacted the DEP to update the amount release to be ~18,900 gallons. Four water trucks off-loading onsite each contained 4,620 gallons of produced fluid. It is estimated that the release traveled 1,143 feet downhill to the stream. A remediation plan is in place, and they are implementing it as we spoke. On 03/23/2026 at 2218 hours the first of five water trucks arrived onsite to off-load fluid for upcoming completion activities. From 2218-0319 hours 4 water trucks off-loaded onsite. At 0615 hours on 03/24/2026 a 5th water truck started offloading and immediately noticed the leak and stopped off-loading. On 03/25/2026 Repsol reported that as of 0700 hours ~10,500 gallons of fluid had been recovered from the stormwater channel and basin. On 03/25/2026 the DEP conducted an incident inspection report of Repsol's UGLIUZZA Well Pad. Water Quality Specialists Korey Starkey, Jonathan Pennings and I arrived at ~ 0930 hours. Licensed Professional Geologist Samuel Louderback arrived at approximately 1100 hours. The DEP met with Repsol representative Meagan DePue and Resource Management. Fenton Excavation was onsite excavating within the LOD to capture fluids during the inspection. Meagan stated that she contacted the PFBC and left a message. She informed us that a hose connected to the manifold was not connected to the produced fluid tanks and that it was hanging over the side of the secondary containment into the stormwater ditch while the first four trucks off-loaded (photo #2-6). The produced fluid then flowed to the stormwater basin (photo #7) and through the drainage pipe of the stormwater basin (photo #9) into a natural conveyance channel which reached a UNT to Rockwell Creek. The DEP, Repsol and Resource Management walked the impacted area together. Resource Management set up monitoring points and split sampled during that time. The fluids in the stormwater ditch were field measured for Electrical Conductivity (EC) at ~7.85 mS/cm. There was a sump pump in the stormwater ditch (photo #5). A sample was collected from the stormwater basin at 1204 hours (photo #8). The EC of the sampled fluids were >19.99 mS/cm. Fluids were able to escape the basin through an outflow pipe. Two sumps were constructed inside and outside of the basin (photo #7 and 10). Fluids collected in the sumps were being actively recovered.The EC of the drainage area beyond the stormwater basin was ~1.8 mS/cm and the soil EC was ~4.8 mS/cm (photo #11). The drainage area forms a conveyance channel ~500ft down from the release location. The EC of the conveyance channel was ~5.4 mS/cm (photo #12). There was a spring adding water to the channel ~900ft downstream from the release location. It was located above grade (photo #13). The EC of the spring was ~100 us/cm. We traveled ~500ft downstream the conveyance channel and obtained EC readings between 2.6-2.7 mS/cm (photo #14 and 15).We traveled downstream ~435ft. The conveyance channel EC was between 5.8-8.0 mS/cm (photo #16 and 17). The DEP and Resource Management each collected a sample at 1053 hours from the UNT upstream of where the released fluids discharged into the stream (photo #18). The DEP and Resource Management each collected a sample at 1118 hours from the UNT downstream of where the released fluids discharged into the stream (photo #22).The EC of Rockwell Creek ~1.4 miles away was ~0.15 mS/cm.

Fluid within containment for the 1009H GPU is observed with conductivity reading of 3.8mS/cm. The Department recommends vacuuming all secondary containment features associated with production equipment. All containment structures are in good repair and are functioning as designed.No new violations noted. Violations still remain outstanding from Inspection Reports 3305227, 3306834, and 3324293.

Comments: This well was drilled in a forested area off of Point View Road in March 2006. Since the most recent inspection of this site on 9/10/2021 (Inspection Record # 3249384), work has continued on remediation of the site, but final restoration has not yet been completed. A spill was reported to the Department on 11:03 AM on August 27, 2021. The spill occurred from a broken copper line attached to the wellhead. The estimated volume lost from this spill was 2 bbl. During this inspection, it was noted that the production equipment remains disconnected and staged along the edge of the site. Stressed vegetation and all contaminated soil associated with the spill has been removed. The NOV response stated that the earth disturbance at the site would be left open until the attainment standards from the alternative remediation process had been demonstrated. The approval of the RACR was mailed to Diversified on 1/10/2022. Violations at the site can be closed when the contaminated soil has been replaced, the site has been graded to final contours and stabilized, and the well has been returned to production.

No new violations noted. Violations remain outstanding from Inspection Reports 3450259 and 3492351.

Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 931176
Permit API: 081-21885
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/27/2021
Comments: This follow-up inspection was conducted in order to assess conditions on both well pads. I inspected Pad A first. The 6 wells on Pad A are still in flowback. Multiple batteries of frac tanks are present within secondary containment. The pad was dry and no issues were noted. On Pad B, drilling is on-going. I met with EQT company man RD Mann uppn arriving on location. Five of the nine wells have already been drilled. In the sump on the pad which had been installed after fluid with elevated electrical conductivity (EC), strontium, and aluminum was discovered, the EC was approximately 800 uS/cm. Two areas of staining were found on the pad and the fluid present here had an EC of approximately 800 uS/cm in both areas. Other puddles on the pad had an EC of approximately 500 uS/cm. The Department recommends scraping these stains from the pad surface and disposing of the material appropriately. I showed Mr. Mann the location of these stains during this inspection and he said that he would have both stains scraped immediately. Violations remain outstanding.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2019-08-07 to Pin Oak Energy Partners Llc in Jones Twp, Elk county. 78.88(d) - OPERATING WELLS - MECHANICAL INTEGRITY OF OPERATING WELLS - Operator failed to immediately notify the Department and take corrective actions to repair or replace defective equipment or casing for wells exhibiting progressive corrosion, rusting or other signs of equipment deterioration that compromise the integrity of the well.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Pin Oak Energy Partners Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2019-08-07
Violation Code: 78.88(d) - OPERATING WELLS - MECHANICAL INTEGRITY OF OPERATING WELLS - Operator failed to immediately notify the Department and take corrective actions to repair or replace defective equipment or casing for wells exhibiting progressive corrosion, rusting or other signs of equipment deterioration that compromise the integrity of the well.
Violation ID: 858211
Permit API: 047-24395
Unconventional: No
County: Elk
Municipality: Jones Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-08-07
Comments: This well is bubbling between the annulus of the 9 5/8" and the 13 3/8". The well was drilled in 2009. The water between the pipes is swirling and has continuous bubbling. There is fluid leaking from the threads on the swedge and into the annulus. I had Jason English come out and test the water and ground around the well and it read over 20.00 mS in the water there is a dead area running away from the well. The well is abandoned and Pin Oak employees told me today that the well was never produced and has been leaking like this for years. There is no gas line to produce the well. Production was reported for 2018. There is 853' of surface casing in this well. The well has 438 psi on it at this time. If the casing is set at 853' (853 x .433 x .80 = 295.4) the well is over-pressured. The meter used to test the conductivity is a ECTester11+ Multi range.

Inspection Date: 3/13/2024
Comments: On March 13 2024, the Department conducted an inspection for the Herminie Well Pad(ESCGP-3 issued on 12/12/2023 expiring on 12/11/2028). Present during today's inspection was operator representative Mr. Duane.The results are as follows:At the time of the inspection the Act 9 sign was present and appeared properly installed. The access road appeared to be stable with no signs of accelerated erosion. The ERP, and PPC plans were present in the onsite mailbox. During today's inspection of the well pad, the operator was actively air drilling well 14H. According to the operator, drilling began the day prior and they are currently at an estimated depth of 20 feet and no other wells had been spud at the time of the inspection. Upon inspection, it appeared not all necessary equipment was with in secondary containment. The Department inquired if additional secondary containment would be installed to which Mr.Duane stated that additional containment would be installed once the big rig moves onto the pad and that there is no secondary containment under the containers where the drilling mud is being discharged into as it is only fresh water and mud. The secondary containment that was observed onsite appeared to be installed correctly with no tears or leaks. No spills were observed on the well pad or with in the secondary containment.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for failure to have proper secondary containment.
